messages:
sara (support): Hi @james — saw your ticket about intermittent 403s when calling the embeddings endpoint from EU region. Can you paste one of the failing request IDs and the approximate local time it happened?

james (customer): Request id: rq_0a9f3b2c, happened ~2024-06-12T15:21:34+01:00. This is streaming embeddings via chunked SSE from our app servers in eu-west, sometimes succeeds, sometimes 403 mid-stream.

sara (support): Thanks — can you also confirm whether you use an edge proxy (nginx/ALB) in front of your app? Any LB timeouts or token rotation?

james (customer): We have nginx reverse proxy on the app nodes (proxy_buffering off, keepalive on). Token is short-lived, rotated by a background job every 10m.

mike (eng): thx for the details. 2 quick asks so we can reproduce: 1) a curl reproduction that mimics your client (SSE + Authorization header + cookie if present), 2) full response headers for the failing request (we need upstream response headers), 3) server-side nginx access/error log lines for rq_0a9f3b2c.

jenna (sre): Also please run a tcpdump or equivalent capturing TLS handshake for a single failure if possible. If capturing TLS is hard, collect the nginx access line with request_time and upstream_response_time. Those numbers help us identify timeout vs auth failure.

james (customer): OK will collect. What's the exact curl you want? Our client uses --no-buffer and raw streaming.

mike (eng): Use this minimal SSE-style curl (no extra libs):

```bash
curl -v --no-buffer \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "X-Client-Region: eu-west" \
  --raw \
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings/stream" \
  -o -
```

Add `-H "Cookie: session=..."` if you send cookies. Replace $REDWOOD_TOKEN with the token used by your app. Keep the -v output (headers) and save to a file.

mike (eng): Important: capture both the client-side curl stdout/stderr and the nginx access.log lines for the same timestamp. We need the response headers that curl prints (HTTP/1.1 403 ... and any x-request-id, x-upstream-id).

jenna (sre): If the 403 happens mid-stream, include the raw bytes around the cutoff (curl -o outfile and include stderr). Also collect nginx error.log for the time range +-30s for the request id.

james (customer): Got it. I'll paste the curl -v output and logs. One more — our infra inserts a custom header X-Client-Nonce set by Envoy. Could that cause anything?

mike (eng): unlikely but include it. Also include any config for token refresh — does your client retry with a new token mid-request? That can cause 403 if new token not accepted by the same connection.

diag-bot: automated hint: You can generate a debug bundle with our helper script: `./tools/collect_debug_bundle.sh --req rq_0a9f3b2c --since 2024-06-12T15:20:00Z --until 2024-06-12T15:25:00Z`. That will package curl output, nginx lines, and tcpdump (if present). Upload link: https://files.redwood.internal/upload/ (expires in 7 days).

james (customer): Uploaded bundle -> https://files.redwood.internal/downloads/abc123. I also attached curl log excerpt:

```
* Rebuilt URL to: https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings/stream
*   Trying 3.112.45.22:443... connected
* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1):
> GET /v1/embeddings/stream HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.example
> User-Agent: curl/7.85.0
> Accept: text/event-stream
> Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
> X-Client-Region: eu-west
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< content-type: text/event-stream
< x-request-id: rq_0a9f3b2c
< x-upstream-id: ups-12
< 
event: data
data: {"embedding": [...]} 

* connection seems to be dead
* Closing connection 0
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS alert, close notify (256):
* SSL: certificate verify ok
* Server returned HTTP status code 403
```

jenna (sre): nice, we see 200 then later "Server returned HTTP status code 403" — indicates server closed with a 403 after initial partial success. Check your nginx logs for a 401/403 from upstream or a 502 from the proxy. Also check whether your token refresh job is swapping tokens mid-connection.

mike (eng): From initial glance the x-upstream-id ups-12 is useful. We'll look for that in our traces. Can you also grep for upstream response headers in your logs for ups-12 around that time?

james (customer): Will do. Anything else I should include to speed this up?

mike (eng): If possible include a short repeatable script that opens multiple concurrent SSE connections to simulate load — sometimes this repros only at scale. Example quick script (bash):

```bash
for i in {1..20}; do \
  curl --no-buffer -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_TOKEN" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
    -H "X-Client-Region: eu-west" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings/stream" &\
done
wait
```

mike (eng): Once we have curl output + nginx access/error logs + bundle, we'll correlate with our runtime traces using x-request-id and x-upstream-id. If you prefer, we can provide a signed temporary token for testing to avoid rotating your prod tokens — ping me and I can generate one.

james (customer): Great, thanks. Uploading the extra logs now, will ping when done. :thumbsup:

sara (support): Thanks @james — keeping this thread updated. We'll assign eng/sre to investigate after we have the bundle. :pray:
